title: Policy Rule (v3)
description: A single action-authorization rule. Strict subset of the Tier-1 policy specification (docs/agentic-aiops-platform/policy-specification.md): action_authz domain only, allow/deny/require_approval outcomes. v2 (SPEC-030) activated the previously reserved require_approval outcome with an explicit approval tier: tier_1 keeps the decision with the session operator (destructive-but-routine), tier_2 requires a designated approver distinct from the requester (critical destructive). v3 (SPEC-074) adds an optional agent-role axis to the match block: agent_roles_any narrows a rule to the closed SPEC-073 agent-role vocabulary (diagnostician/orchestrator/executor) and composes conjunctively with roles_any (the human token roles). The revision is additive and inert — absent agent_roles_any means unconstrained, so every v2 rule validates and evaluates byte-identically under v3, and no deployed caller threads an agent-role until a later phase. allow_with_conditions and conditions remain reserved for a future schema revision.

domain.description: Policy domain. Only action_authz is supported.

description.description: Short human-readable explanation of the rule.

priority.description: Numeric precedence. Higher wins between rules of the same outcome class (allows, or require_approvals); explicit deny always overrides require_approval and allow; require_approval overrides allow.

enabled.description: Whether the rule participates in evaluation.

roles_any.description: Rule matches if the principal holds any of these roles.

actions_any.description: Rule matches if the requested action is one of these.

agent_roles_any.description: Optional agent-role axis (SPEC-074, v3). Rule matches only if the call carries one of these SPEC-073 agent-roles; composes conjunctively with roles_any. Absent means unconstrained (the rule matches regardless of agent-role), so every v2 rule is byte-identical under v3. A rule that sets this key never matches an unscoped call carrying no agent-role (fail-closed). The axis narrows only — it can never widen what the human token roles already permit.

outcome.description: Decision outcome. Evaluation precedence is deny > require_approval > allow. allow_with_conditions is reserved for a future schema revision.

approval.description: Approval requirement. Mandatory on require_approval outcomes, forbidden on allow/deny outcomes. Tier semantics mirror the authorization matrix: tier_1 = the session operator may decide their own confirmation; tier_2 = a designated approver distinct from the requester decides.

tier.description: Approval level. tier_1: destructive-but-routine, session-operator self-confirmation allowed by default. tier_2: critical destructive, self-approval forbidden by default.

decided_by_roles.description: Roles whose holders may decide the confirmation. Synthetic/workload identities are excluded by authoring, not by code.

allow_self_approval.description: Optional override of the tier default. Unset means the tier default: tier_1 allows self-approval, tier_2 forbids it. tier_2 with explicit true is rejected at bundle load.
